title: Sufficiency of Scripture
definition: The sufficiency of Scripture means that God's written Word contains all that He intends His people to have as the final authority for salvation, doctrine, godliness, correction, and faithful obedience.
summary: Scripture is sufficient because God has spoken with purpose and wisdom. The church does not need a higher authority beside Scripture, nor a competing source of doctrine above Scripture. The Word of God is enough to reveal the Gospel, guide faith, train righteousness, and equip God's people for every good work.
christFocus: The sufficiency of Scripture rests in the sufficiency of Christ. Scripture faithfully reveals who Christ is, what He has done, and how His people are to follow Him until He returns.

studySections.heading: Enough for Salvation
studySections.content: Scripture reveals the truth of sin, grace, faith, repentance, Christ's saving work, and eternal life. It gives the testimony God intends His people to believe concerning salvation.

studySections.heading: Enough for Doctrine
studySections.content: Christian doctrine must be built from the Word of God. Scripture is sufficient to establish what the church must teach, guard, confess, and pass on.

studySections.heading: Enough for Godly Living
studySections.content: Scripture equips the believer for every good work. It corrects, trains, warns, comforts, and guides God's people into faithful obedience.

studySections.heading: Sufficiency Does Not Reject Helps
studySections.content: Teachers, commentaries, creeds, dictionaries, and study tools can be useful servants, but they are not masters. Every resource must remain under Scripture's authority.

sources: Scripture references listed in this doctrine entry.
